$comment: Cursor's docs now present `agent` as the primary command, but the installer still ships `cursor-agent` and `agent` is far too generic a name to probe for (`command -v agent` can false-positive on unrelated binaries). `cursor-agent` remains supported as the stable alias, so it is both the probe target and the launch binary.

none.label: Default
none.summary: Asks before commands; edits go through.
none.description: Cursor with no permission flag: it asks before commands its allowlist does not cover, and applies file edits in the workspace without asking.

auto.$comment: Cursor's own auto mode. `cursor-agent --help`: `--auto-review  Use Auto-review (Smart Auto): a server classifier auto-runs safe tool calls and prompts for the rest`. No `manual` is declared: Cursor applies file edits in the workspace without asking whatever flag it gets, so it cannot be held to asking before every change.
auto.label: Auto-review
auto.summary: Cursor runs what it judges safe; asks for the rest.
auto.description: Cursor’s own auto-review: a classifier runs the tool calls it judges safe and asks for the rest.

bypass.$comment: `--yolo` is documented as an alias for `--force`; only one is sent.
bypass.label: Run Everything
bypass.description: Cursor’s Run Everything (--force): every command runs without asking unless your rules deny it. Use only in repositories you trust.

modelSelection.$comment: Headline ids from `cursor-agent --list-models` (verified against CLI 2026.09.10). The CLI already takes `--model`; the picker was empty because this seed listed nothing. Cursor encodes effort and fast in the slug itself (`composer-2.5-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`), so this is a curated set — Auto, Cursor's own models, and one default-effort slug per major vendor — not the full entitlement-expanded roster. allowCustomId stays true so Settings can add a slug the plan actually has.

resume.$comment: Cursor documents `--resume <chat-id>` and `--continue` (previous session). Mirrors the OpenCode wiring: --continue as the base, the explicit resume pair only when the caller has an id. Unverified end-to-end, so capabilities.resumeSession stays false until confirmed against a real install (the confirm-first discipline).

promptInjection.$comment: The first message goes after `--`, so one that starts with a dash is never read as an option. Checked 2026-10-22 against Cursor Agent 2026.10.14: `cursor-agent --bogus` failed with `unknown option`, and `cursor-agent -- --version` took `--version` as the prompt (it asked to sign in rather than printing the version).

overflow.$comment: cursor-agent 2026.09.15 documents no prompt-file option and no stdin prompt for an interactive session (-p/--prompt is a one-shot print mode), so a first message too long for the platform's command line is typed in: launched without it, then pasted (bracketed) and submitted once the TUI is reading. Verified 2026-09-24 that the composer takes the bracketed paste once the TUI has enabled bracketed paste and gone quiet.

contextInjection.$comment: cursor-agent 2026.09.10 documents no --append-system-prompt flag (verified against --help). The hidden --system-prompt REPLACES the stock prompt and is team-gated, so it is not this channel. --plugin-dir is the public out-of-band path: the host packs the document as a one-session Cursor plugin (always-apply rule under .cursor-plugin/) and that directory is what {{contextFile}} names. Writing .cursor/rules into the person's repo is deliberately not the channel. Spread into launch AND resume argv, so a resumed session is re-told — plugin rules load per invocation, and sessionStart does not re-fire on --continue.

mcpConfig.$comment: Cursor reads workspace MCP servers from .cursor/mcp.json in the same {"mcpServers": {...}} shape Claude Code uses, so the claude-code writer applies as-is.

launchIntegration.$comment: The gateway, the person's synced MCP servers and a launch skill ride one more --plugin-dir (rendered into integrationArgs) instead of .cursor/mcp.json and .cursor/skills. Measured against cursor-agent 2026.10.14 on 2026-10-16: a plugin's .mcp.json server starts with no server-approval dialog (a project .cursor/mcp.json one stops the start at one), the flag is repeatable beside the host-context plugin, and skills/<id>/SKILL.md loads. The agent-state hook is NOT in the plugin: a plugin's stop and beforeSubmitPrompt hooks fire only when the person's or the project's own hooks file names the same event, so it is registered in the user-level ~/.cursor/hooks.json instead (agentStateSpec).

agentStateSpec.$comment: Cursor's CLI ships lifecycle hooks (2026-01-16 CLI update): project-level .cursor/hooks.json in the flat {version, hooks: {<event>: [{command}]}} shape, camelCase event names, snake_case stdin payload with hook_event_name/conversation_id/transcript_path base fields (conversation_id is the resume chat id; the shared reporter forwards it as the session id). awaiting_input is DELIBERATELY unsupported: Cursor has no Notification/PermissionRequest-style event — its permission flow consults beforeShellExecution/beforeMCPExecution hooks, which fire on every tool run and whose empty-stdout response semantics are unverified, so registering a reporter there risks interfering with approvals rather than observing them. Until verified against a real install (rides kimi-cursor-e2e-verification), a Cursor permission prompt reads as its last working phase and the stall watchdog is the backstop. stop's payload carries status completed|aborted|error — all three end the turn (idle+turnEnd), and error/aborted additionally flag the turn FAILED via failureWhen, so an automation run whose Cursor turn crashes or is interrupted finalizes as failed instead of opening a PR from unfinished work. Agent changelists: Cursor's postToolUse payload carries no file edit, so afterFileEdit is registered too (phase thinking, mid-turn) — it is the only event that names the file and its old/new strings, from which the reporter locates the changed line ranges. Payload shape READ OFF the shipped cursor-agent 2026.09.08 bundle: the base payload is {hook_event_name, session_id (falling back to conversation_id), cursor_version, workspace_roots:[workspacePath], user_email, transcript_path} and afterFileEdit adds file_path plus edits[] whose {old_string, new_string} are one hunk's '-' and '+' lines joined — no context, so a hunk that only DELETES has an empty new_string and cannot be located, which costs that call its line ranges and leaves a file-level claim. Not verified end-to-end (cursor-agent refuses headless without an account: "Not logged in").

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (the confirm-first discipline); the resume argv above is wired for the flip. sessionIdFromCaller is false because Cursor mints its own chat ids (no --session-id-style launch assignment is documented).
